Career platform quality contract

Canonical branch: main
Canonical validation entry point: npm run site:verify
Complete local verification entry point: npm run site:local
Local release runbook: docs/LOCAL_RELEASE_RUNBOOK.md
Source completion record: docs/audits/SITE_SOURCE_COMPLETION_2026-07-16.md
Automated release workflow: .github/workflows/site-build.yml
Manual diagnostic workflow: .github/workflows/site-diagnostics.yml
Historical PR 9 recovery audit: docs/audits/PR_9_RECOVERY_AUDIT.md
Complete PR 1-16 recovery audit: docs/audits/PR_1_16_RECOVERY_AUDIT.md
Verbatim PR file archive: docs/audits/pr-artifacts/PR_1_16_FILE_ARCHIVE.md
Identity and work-mode audit: docs/audits/COPY_IDENTITY_AND_WORK_MODES_AUDIT_2026-07-16.md
Comprehensive closure matrix: docs/audits/CAREER_PLATFORM_10_OF_10_CLOSURE_MATRIX.md

The release contract covers:
- zero-warning ESLint, strict TypeScript, and source-level career boundaries
- one coherent professional identity with explicit personal working style
- sustained internal-role ownership versus bounded commercial engagements
- visible contact self-routing, standard-form fallback, and neutral generic navigation
- one canonical engagement catalogue and synchronized India/global pricing state
- audited product maturity, evidence provenance, and freshness
- accessibility, contrast, reduced motion, print, privacy, and machine-readable profiles
- accessible section navigation across Home, About, Experience, Services, Work, Proof, and Book
- route-aware hiring, services, and book conversion paths
- same-origin Three.js runtime, resilient product-lab fallback, and portable module syntax validation
- generated resume, publication package, social previews, static budgets, redirects, sitemap, and internal links
- protected publication artifacts are restored from the current Git HEAD when missing, without overwriting existing files
- deployment-ready static export after publication-only assets are pruned
- local HTTP smoke testing of the generated static export and build identity
- an exact-commit `canonical-site-verify` status with retained verification log and export artifact
- a main-only diagnostic workflow with read-only permissions, retained artifacts, and a 15-minute timeout
- explicit closure criteria across identity, hiring, commercial work, evidence, transactions, measurement, accessibility, discovery, legal trust, deployment, and production learning
- full-file and review-thread recovery evidence for every pull request created before the main-only rule was enforced

Operating rule:
- all portfolio work is integrated directly on main
- automated release checks run only for main pushes or explicit manual dispatch
- the automated workflow validates the exact triggering SHA, not a later moving branch head
- no pull request is treated as canonical work or as a required verification surface
- before closing an existing pull request, compare it with current main and carry forward every missing or better file, contract, check, document, or review finding
- documentation recovered from a pull request must be preserved on main without hard-coded source revisions that become stale immediately
- rejected workflows are preserved only as non-executable audit artifacts
- after recovery and validation, obsolete pull requests are closed and their branches are deleted
- do not deploy an export that has not passed npm run site:local
- do not reopen generic source redesign work without failed verification, production evidence, direct product evidence, or observed user behavior
- prefer one canonical validation path; automated and diagnostic workflows must call that path rather than reproduce a second validation pipeline
